finding.claim: reset_password_loose compares the stored reset token to the user-supplied token with loose equality (==). If $token arrives as a JSON boolean true (or int 0 on PHP<8), it matches any stored string token. Numeric-string collisions such as '0e123' == '0e456' also match. An attacker can bypass token validation and reset any user's password.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled $token and $email parameters (e.g. from a password-reset request body, possibly JSON-decoded so types are attacker-controlled)
finding.sink: UPDATE users SET pw = ... WHERE email = ... (line 5-6), which sets the victim's password

trace.note: Fetches the stored token for the attacker-chosen email
$row['token'] == $token uses PHP loose comparison, which is type-juggling-prone and not constant-time
Password overwritten for the victim's email on a loose match

finding.guards_checked: No type check on $token and no strict (===) or hash_equals comparison. SQL injection is guarded by $db->quote(). The sibling reset_password() uses hash_equals with a string cast, so it is not affected by this issue. I could not see the callers, so exploitability depends on the token type reaching this function.

verdict.guard_found: none on $token in reset.php (no type declaration, no strict comparison). The SQL is guarded by $db->quote() at lines 3, 5 and 6. The sibling reset_password() at line 14 uses hash_equals with a (string) cast.
verdict.reason: The loose `==` at reset.php:4 is real, and `true == "abc"` passes in PHP, but the only file here is reset.php and nothing calls reset_password_loose, so I can't tell whether $token can reach it as a non-string (e.g. a JSON bool).

finding.claim: Neither reset function expires the reset token or deletes it after use, and the resets table has no expiry check. A leaked or old token stays valid and can be replayed indefinitely to reset the password again.
finding.source: A previously issued or leaked reset token plus the victim's email

trace.note: Selects the token only; no created_at or expiry column is read
Token is verified, but nothing marks it as used
Password updated; there is no DELETE on resets and no session invalidation

finding.guards_checked: hash_equals gives a constant-time compare. There is no expiry check, no single-use enforcement and no rate limiting in this file. Callers were not available to check for controls there.

verdict.guard_found: hash_equals constant-time compare at reset.php:14 (only checks equality). No expiry, single-use deletion, or rate limiting in this file; callers not available.
verdict.reason: reset.php:13 selects only the token, :14 compares it, and :15-16 update the password with no DELETE or expiry check on resets, so a stale or leaked token can be replayed by an anonymous attacker. Both functions (including reset_password_loose at :4) have the same flaw.
